doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Bass, piano and guitar in Latin music
summary: Why the bass must know Latin style, Rendón's bassists, and his uncertainty about guitar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I would imagine you’ve got to have a bass player who really knows this music.

Because the first time I tried to at least absorb some of this Latin music and much of it where the bass is anticipating, and it just seemed so incorrect. We’re used to jazz, we’re used to walking bass, we’re hitting the downbeats, even if it’s a funky thing usually.

Well it happened yesterday, the young man caught on very quickly, but I had to tell him [scats] and then he went down to [scats] which is good too, that’s an older style as I mentioned to him. And that worked out very nicely what he was doing. But yes you have to be very knowledgeable. I have a bass player that played with Tito Puente for many years and he played with Rubén Blades, I don’t know if you know that particular name. But he’s very experienced in the field for the past fifteen years or so. And then the one I have today — he couldn’t make it because he already had a gig. I have Ian Stewart, so I think he’s come here he told me, he’s from here. He’s a young man, early 30s, he’s got a lot of experience already. He wrote a book with John Benitez on Latino bass playing. So he’s very knowledgeable, so he plays with the band periodically. So yes. Also, the same thing with the piano players, they have to know how to play with the percussion and the rhythm and the bass player. The one that I’m not very good at is the guitar. I have to learn more. Because the guitar is kind of tricky because they have to play with the piano but

not necessarily the same thing so how do you do it without getting in the way. So that’s one thing that I haven’t looked into you know, that much. I depend on them to sort of do it, if I happen to use a guitar player.
